title: Memory page: choose the structure
question: The world is the WireCat patch rack. Which arrangement should the Memory page take? Keep the roll, take another, or re-roll.

options.label: The ledger
options.lineage: an account ledger: one line per entry, newest on top, grouped by day
options.thesis: Everything agents and you wrote into memory, as one dated ledger. A proposed entry carries an amber lamp and waits for Confirm; a confirmed one turns green in place.
options.viewport: Title Memory, a one-line count of what waits for you, a segmented filter (Waiting / Kept / Past / All), then the rack: Today, Yesterday, Oct 28... Each row: lamp, kind, the memory text, who wrote it, one action.
options.risk: Time order hides what a person is about; a long history becomes a scroll.

options.label: Waiting, then kept
options.thesis: Two racks: what waits for your decision on top, what is kept below, grouped by kind. Trust comes from clearing the top rack.
options.viewport: Title, then a 'Waiting for you' rack with amber rows and Confirm buttons, then a 'Kept' rack.
options.risk: Two racks break the one-rack-per-page rule; a confirmed row has to move between racks, which rule 9 forbids.

options.label: Query and facets
options.thesis: A query bar in memo's own query language with facets for status, kind, scope and author, over one table, exactly like Logs.
options.viewport: Title, query bar, facets on the left, a table of records on the right.
options.risk: Built for an expert with thousands of rows; the owner has a handful and needs a decision, not a search.
